hypotheses.construction_plan: Define L(t)=F(x*y + t*z). Rewrite x*(y+z) as x*y + x*z; then the first F-call is L(x) and the second F-call is L(w). The original expression is the sum L(x)+L(w).
hypotheses.rationale: Both F arguments share the same x*y term and differ only in the coefficient multiplying z, so they are evaluations of a common one-parameter family in that coefficient.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Treat the argument of F as a linear form in the basis (y,z). The first argument expands to x*y+x*z, giving coefficient vector (x,x); the second argument gives coefficient vector (x,w). The original expression is the sum of F applied to these two coefficient vectors.
required_assumptions: The arguments of F are linear combinations of y and z
hypotheses.rationale: Both expressions are F applied to linear forms in y and z, so their coefficient vectors form a reduced latent representation of the shared structure.
